evals.prompt: This Node.js project has no CI yet. Set up continuous integration that runs our lint and test scripts.
evals.expected_output: A GitHub Actions workflow in .github/workflows that follows the ci skill rules.
expectations: A workflow file is created under .github/workflows/ and no other CI system's config is introduced
It triggers on pull_request and on push to the default branch, plus workflow_dispatch
Top-level permissions are set to contents: read
Dependency caching is enabled and concurrency with cancel-in-progress and a job timeout-minutes are set
Action versions were looked up and pinned to a current major version rather than guessed from memory

evals.prompt: We want CI on GitLab CI for our new service. Write the pipeline config.
evals.expected_output: The assistant does not silently introduce a non-GitHub CI system.
expectations: The assistant recognises the user explicitly asked for GitLab CI and either honours that request or confirms it
It does not substitute GitHub Actions without saying so
If the project already used another CI system, it asks before migrating instead of rewriting

evals.prompt: Add a release workflow that deploys to production and uses our API token.
evals.expected_output: A release workflow using secrets and environments safely.
expectations: The token is read from GitHub Actions secrets, never written into a file in the repository
The deploy job uses a GitHub environment, with required reviewers recommended for production
Extra permissions are granted per job rather than at the top level
The workflow calls a repository script or task rather than embedding long inline logic
